action_items: FIX (MEDIUM): LoanPassbookCard has button-inside-button HTML structure violation. Line 221 is outer <button> that contains ExternalLink <button> at line 245. Change outer element to <div role='button'> or restructure layout to avoid nesting. This triggers React hydration warnings in browser console.
critical_code_review_comments: MEDIUM: ClientDetail.jsx LoanPassbookCard - outer loan card toggle is <button> (line 221) containing inner ExternalLink <button> (line 245). Invalid HTML5 - button cannot contain button. Console shows: 'In HTML, <button> cannot be a descendant of <button>'. Fix: change outer button to div with cursor-pointer and onClick.

LOW: fetchLoans uses useCallback with [id, loans] dependency - since loans starts as null and updates to array, the dependency is correctly preventing re-fetch (loans !== null check). However, the useCallback dependency on loans means a new function reference is created after first fetch. Consider using a ref-based approach for the 'already fetched' check.

OK: kyc_id filter correctly added to GET /api/loans - works for all roles (admin returns {}, sipahi/muneem use assigned_illaka_ids). The kyc_id filter is ANDed with the role-based query, which is correct behavior.
OK: LoanPassbookCard manages optimistic state updates - on collect, uses updated loan from API response; on undo, refetches loan from GET /api/loans/{id}. Consistent with server state.

LOW: DELETE /api/loans/{id}/payments/{pid} - passbook undo uses emi_month as pid (e.g. '2026-04'). The path parameter naming is 'pid' but it's actually an emi_month string. This works but is slightly misleading.

rca_of_issue: HTML button-inside-button: In LoanPassbookCard, the loan header toggle button (line 221) wraps the ExternalLink button (line 245). HTML5 spec prohibits interactive content (button) inside interactive content (button). Browser silently restructures DOM causing React hydration mismatch. Fix: change outer element from <button> to <div> with onClick and role='button' styling, keeping same visual/click behavior.
